# Resolver refusals — a table of (profile selection -> exact refusal text).
# Regenerate with: go test ./internal/policy -update
# Every case here used to be ACCEPTED; read INDEX.md §3.4 before
# changing any line below — a change here is a change to the security boundary.

== symlink_conflict_different_targets ==
conflict at /custom/tool: symlink to vendor-a (from link-a) and to vendor-b (from link-b).
       A symlink has one target; profiles may only ever grant, so neither may
       silently repoint the other's. Select one of the two.

== symlink_cannot_repoint_sys_bin ==
conflict at /bin: symlink to usr/sbin (from 0shadow) and to usr/bin (from @sys).
       A symlink has one target; profiles may only ever grant, so neither may
       silently repoint the other's. Select one of the two.

== join_conflict_different_content ==
conflict at /generated: two different generated contents (from gen-a and from gen-b)

== join_conflict_different_perms ==
conflict at /generated: mode 0600 (from gen-a) and 0644 (from gen-b)

== grant_at_root_tmpfs ==
profile takeroot puts an empty tmpfs at /, but the sandbox root is snug's own:
       it is already an empty tmpfs, and the masking rule cannot see inside a grant
       at / — nothing above it can be judged. Grant the paths you meant instead.

== grant_at_root_ro ==
profile takeroot puts a bind of /opt at /, but the sandbox root is snug's own:
       it is already an empty tmpfs, and the masking rule cannot see inside a grant
       at / — nothing above it can be judged. Grant the paths you meant instead.

== grant_at_exactly_proc ==
profile claim puts a bind of /opt at /proc, but /proc is snug's own: it must be a fresh procfs bound to the sandbox's OWN pid namespace, or the sandbox reads the host's process table.
       Whatever a profile puts there takes it over — by displacing the node snug
       authors, or, where snug mounts nothing at all, by being a separate mount that
       --remount-ro / does not reach inside. Either way it is a hole no profile may
       open.
       Remove the grant. snug mounts a procfs at /proc in every sandbox, so there
       is nothing a profile needs to add there.

== grant_at_exactly_dev ==
profile claim puts a bind of /opt at /dev, but /dev is snug's own: it must be bwrap's synthetic minimal device set, never a bind of the host's (which hands over every block device and every input device).
       Whatever a profile puts there takes it over — by displacing the node snug
       authors, or, where snug mounts nothing at all, by being a separate mount that
       --remount-ro / does not reach inside. Either way it is a hole no profile may
       open.
       Remove the grant. snug mounts bwrap's device tree at /dev in every sandbox;
       one more device node is a change to snug, not a grant a profile can make.

== grant_at_snugdir_tmpfs ==
profile claim puts an empty tmpfs at /snug, but /snug is snug's own: it is the namespace snug reserves for everything it needs a path for inside a sandbox — /snug/bin among them — and those paths are unwritable only because they are plain directories on the root tmpfs that --remount-ro / covers. A mount here takes /snug/bin with it, and snug puts that directory FIRST on PATH.
       Whatever a profile puts there takes it over — by displacing the node snug
       authors, or, where snug mounts nothing at all, by being a separate mount that
       --remount-ro / does not reach inside. Either way it is a hole no profile may
       open.
       Grant the path you actually meant — any path that neither is nor contains
       /snug. Nothing a profile needs lives there; it is snug's own.

== grant_at_stagedbindir_tmpfs ==
profile claim puts an empty tmpfs at /snug/bin, but /snug/bin is snug's own: it is a plain directory on the root tmpfs, which is what makes it unwritable once / is remounted read-only, and snug puts it FIRST on PATH. A mount at or above it is not covered by that remount, so it would hand the payload a writable directory ahead of /usr/bin.
       Whatever a profile puts there takes it over — by displacing the node snug
       authors, or, where snug mounts nothing at all, by being a separate mount that
       --remount-ro / does not reach inside. Either way it is a hole no profile may
       open.
       Stage the FILE, never the directory:
         ro = ["/host/path/tool:/snug/bin/tool"]
       If you named an ancestor because something inside needs a writable runtime
       directory, grant THAT directory — any path that neither is nor contains
       /snug/bin.

== grant_inside_snugdir_unplaced_path ==
profile claim puts an empty tmpfs at /snug/engine, inside snug's own namespace /snug:
       the ONE thing a profile may do there is stage a single executable read-only
       under /snug/bin, which is what that directory exists for. Anything else — a tmpfs, a
       writable bind, or a mount AT one of the directories snug creates — either
       displaces something snug put there or escapes --remount-ro / and becomes a
       writable directory ahead of /usr/bin on the PATH snug hands over.
       Stage the FILE, never the directory:
         ro = ["/host/path/tool:/snug/bin/tool"]

== grant_at_legacy_snugdir ==
profile claim puts a bind of /opt at /run/snug/bin/tool, but snug's own paths moved from /run/snug to /snug
       (issue #206), and /run/snug is kept refused so this grant cannot silently stop
       working. A staging grant there would still validate, stage into a directory
       that is no longer on PATH, and say nothing.
       Stage into the new location instead:
         ro = ["/host/path/tool:/snug/bin/tool"]
       If you wanted an unrelated runtime directory rather than snug's, pick a path
       outside /run/snug — that name is a tombstone now, not a feature.

== grant_at_snugdir_bind ==
profile claim puts a bind of /opt at /snug, but /snug is snug's own: it is the namespace snug reserves for everything it needs a path for inside a sandbox — /snug/bin among them — and those paths are unwritable only because they are plain directories on the root tmpfs that --remount-ro / covers. A mount here takes /snug/bin with it, and snug puts that directory FIRST on PATH.
       Whatever a profile puts there takes it over — by displacing the node snug
       authors, or, where snug mounts nothing at all, by being a separate mount that
       --remount-ro / does not reach inside. Either way it is a hole no profile may
       open.
       Grant the path you actually meant — any path that neither is nor contains
       /snug. Nothing a profile needs lives there; it is snug's own.

== grant_strictly_inside_proc ==
profile nest puts a bind of /opt at /proc/sys, which is inside /proc — a pseudo-filesystem the kernel and bwrap populate, not a grant any profile made.
       That hides what /proc already exposes there, and substitutes host content for kernel
       content: it must be a fresh procfs bound to the sandbox's OWN pid namespace, or the sandbox reads the host's process table.
       Remove the grant at /proc/sys.

== grant_strictly_inside_dev ==
profile nest puts a bind of /opt at /dev/null, which is inside /dev — a pseudo-filesystem the kernel and bwrap populate, not a grant any profile made.
       That hides what /dev already exposes there, and substitutes host content for kernel
       content: it must be bwrap's synthetic minimal device set, never a bind of the host's (which hands over every block device and every input device).
       Remove the grant at /dev/null.

== grant_strictly_inside_resolv_conf ==
profile nest puts a bind of /opt at /etc/resolv.conf/x, which is inside /etc/resolv.conf — a generated FILE (from (snug)).
       A grant beneath a file is meaningless: nothing can be mounted inside a regular file.
       Remove the grant at /etc/resolv.conf/x.

== scalar_conflict_address ==
profiles "addr-a" and "addr-b" set different network addresses (10.0.0.2/24 and 10.0.0.3/24); select only one.
       This key has no permissive direction — there is no "more open" address — so snug
       refuses rather than choosing. Picking one would make the answer depend on the order
       profiles are folded, and the model has no such order.

== scalar_conflict_gateway ==
profiles "gw-a" and "gw-b" set different network gateways (10.0.0.1 and 10.0.0.9); select only one.
       This key has no permissive direction — there is no "more open" address — so snug
       refuses rather than choosing. Picking one would make the answer depend on the order
       profiles are folded, and the model has no such order.

== scalar_conflict_mtu ==
profiles "mtu-a" and "mtu-b" set different MTUs (1400 and 9000); select only one.
       This key has no permissive direction — there is no "more open" address — so snug
       refuses rather than choosing. Picking one would make the answer depend on the order
       profiles are folded, and the model has no such order.

== scalar_conflict_address_forging ==
profile "addr-a": network address 10.0.0.2/24 \u202eSSERDDA-NA-YB-DEGROF does not parse as an address/prefix (e.g. "10.13.13.2/24"): netip.ParsePrefix("10.0.0.2/24 \u202eSSERDDA-NA-YB-DEGROF"): bad bits after slash: "24 \u202eSSERDDA-NA-YB-DEGROF"

== poststaging_nested_grant_under_later_replace ==
profile hostile puts a bind of /opt at /home/u/.claude.json/evil, which is inside /home/u/.claude.json — a generated FILE (from @claude).
       A grant beneath a file is meaningless: nothing can be mounted inside a regular file.
       Remove the grant at /home/u/.claude.json/evil.

== forbidden_env_unset_on_host ==
profile "bad": environ.inherit on LD_PRELOAD, which is a list. Inheriting a host search path wholesale imports directories the sandbox does not have — use environ.sanitise, which copies the host value and keeps only the elements policy grants

== graft_covers_stagedbindir_ancestor_snugdir ==
cannot graft /snug into the engine's view: /snug is snug's own: it is the namespace snug reserves for everything it needs a path for inside a sandbox — /snug/bin among them — and those paths are unwritable only because they are plain directories on the root tmpfs that --remount-ro / covers. A mount here takes /snug/bin with it, and snug puts that directory FIRST on PATH.
       A graft at that path would displace it in the ENGINE's mount namespace
       exactly as a profile's grant would displace it in the sandbox's — this is a
       hole no graft may open, snug's own code included. Graft a destination that
       is neither /snug nor an ancestor of it.

== graft_inside_snugdir_socket ==
cannot graft /snug/podman.sock into the engine's view: it is inside snug's own
       namespace /snug, and the only part of it a graft may land in is the engine's own
       subtree under /snug/engine/.
       Everything else there belongs to the PAYLOAD — the staging directory and the
       proxy sockets — and a graft at one of those replaces it in the engine's mount
       namespace with whatever this graft's source is.

== graft_inside_snugdir_unplaced_path ==
cannot graft /snug/whatever into the engine's view: it is inside snug's own
       namespace /snug, and the only part of it a graft may land in is the engine's own
       subtree under /snug/engine/.
       Everything else there belongs to the PAYLOAD — the staging directory and the
       proxy sockets — and a graft at one of those replaces it in the engine's mount
       namespace with whatever this graft's source is.

== graft_at_legacy_snugdir ==
cannot graft /run/snug/bin into the engine's view: snug's own paths moved from
       /run/snug to /snug (issue #206), and the old location is kept refused so that nothing
       names it by habit. The engine's own destinations are under /snug/engine/.

== graft_covers_stagedbindir_exact ==
cannot graft /snug/bin into the engine's view: /snug/bin is snug's own: it is a plain directory on the root tmpfs, which is what makes it unwritable once / is remounted read-only, and snug puts it FIRST on PATH. A mount at or above it is not covered by that remount, so it would hand the payload a writable directory ahead of /usr/bin.
       A graft at that path would displace it in the ENGINE's mount namespace
       exactly as a profile's grant would displace it in the sandbox's — this is a
       hole no graft may open, snug's own code included. Graft a destination that
       is neither /snug/bin nor an ancestor of it.

== graft_destination_does_not_exist_etc_containers ==
snug cannot graft /etc/containers into the engine's view: nothing in this policy
       creates that directory inside the sandbox, and the sandbox root is read-only, so
       the mkdir that a graft needs fails with EROFS (measured, ENGINE-NETNS.md §5.1).
       Graft a destination that already exists — a path some grant mounts, an ancestor
       of one, or a path inside a writable grant.

== graft_destination_does_not_exist_var_tmp ==
snug cannot graft /var/tmp into the engine's view: nothing in this policy
       creates that directory inside the sandbox, and the sandbox root is read-only, so
       the mkdir that a graft needs fails with EROFS (measured, ENGINE-NETNS.md §5.1).
       Graft a destination that already exists — a path some grant mounts, an ancestor
       of one, or a path inside a writable grant.

== graft_source_not_visible_xdg_runtime_dir ==
cannot graft /home/u/proj/sub/xdg (host /run/user/1000) into the engine's view: the sandbox's own
       policy does not expose this host path, and snug did not create it for this run.
       A graft may only reach a host path the sandbox's OWN grants already expose — the
       engine's view is DERIVED from the sandbox's, never a second, wider window onto
       the host — or a path snug itself created (the container store, the runroot, a
       socket directory), or this run's recorded engine toolchain root, read-only.
       Grant it to the sandbox first, or graft a path snug owns.

== graft_covers_graft ==
cannot graft /home/u/proj/sub/nest into the engine's view: it would CONTAIN the graft
       already at /home/u/proj/sub/nest/child (from (snug)).
       A graft at an ancestor takes the descendant's destination with it in the
       engine's mount namespace — the same containment rule the sandbox's own
       grants follow. Graft a destination that neither is nor contains /home/u/proj/sub/nest/child.

== graft_optional_forbidden ==
cannot graft /home/u/proj/sub/optional-probe: Optional is not permitted on a graft.
       -try semantics mean "silently do less", and under Tier C the derived view IS
       the enforcement boundary — a graft that silently did not happen would leave the
       engine with a different confinement from the one --dry-run described
       (invariant 5). Make the host path exist, or do not graft it.

== graft_empty_why ==
cannot graft /home/u/proj/sub/why-probe: Why is empty.
       Every graft carries the abuse sentence — "a hostile process inside the sandbox
       can use this to ___" — because a graft is the one grant a profile can never
       write, so a Graft literal is the only place left for a human to read it. Set Why
       before calling Policy.Graft.

== graft_source_symlink_escapes_the_sandbox ==
cannot graft /home/u/proj/sub/resolve-probe (host /home/u/secrets) into the engine's view: the sandbox's own
       policy does not expose this host path, and snug did not create it for this run.
       A graft may only reach a host path the sandbox's OWN grants already expose — the
       engine's view is DERIVED from the sandbox's, never a second, wider window onto
       the host — or a path snug itself created (the container store, the runroot, a
       socket directory), or this run's recorded engine toolchain root, read-only.
       Grant it to the sandbox first, or graft a path snug owns.
       The source was named as /home/u/proj/sub/link, which is a SYMLINK on the host;
       snug judges what it resolves to, because open_tree(2) follows it (measured, issue #55).

== graft_guest_control_character ==
graft destination "/home/u/proj/sub/guest-forge-probe\u202eDEGROF" (from (snug)) has '\u202e' in its path the ENGINE VIEW block, and a directional formatting character reverses the rest of the line, so it renders as content it does not contain.
       Every line of `snug --dry-run` is one row, so a path that spans two lines can forge
       a row that does not otherwise exist. No mountpoint needs one; write the path you meant.

== graft_source_control_character ==
graft source "/home/u/proj/sub/source-forge-probe\u202eDEGROF" (from (snug)) has '\u202e' in its path the ENGINE VIEW block, and a directional formatting character reverses the rest of the line, so it renders as content it does not contain.
       Every line of `snug --dry-run` is one row, so a path that spans two lines can forge
       a row that does not otherwise exist. No mountpoint needs one; write the path you meant.

== graft_from_wears_the_sigil ==
cannot graft /home/u/proj/sub/sigil-probe: From is ["@podman-socket"], and a graft's From must be exactly
       []string{"(snug)"}.
       No profile may author a graft — there is no TOML key that produces one, and
       Policy.Graft is the only writer of p.Grafts — so any other From, including the
       name of a builtin this run never selected, means the caller copied provenance
       from somewhere else instead of writing the graft's own. Set From to
       []string{"(snug)"}.

== graft_kind_not_in_the_table ==
cannot graft /home/u/proj/sub/kind-probe: Kind is "bind", and a graft's Kind must be one the engine's
       derived view actually builds — KindGraft (an open_tree(2) clone of a host path),
       or KindProc, KindCgroup2 or KindTmpfs (a fresh mount the stage makes itself). A
       caller building a Graft with any other Kind is a bug in that caller, not a policy
       this can accept.

== graft_fresh_mount_carries_a_host ==
cannot graft /proc: Kind is "proc", which the stage builds as a FRESH mount,
       but Host is "/home/u/.ssh" — a path nothing will ever open.
       A fresh procfs or cgroup2 has no source: the stage mounts it, it does not clone
       a host subtree with open_tree(2). Leaving the field set would put `from /home/u/.ssh` on
       the ENGINE VIEW block for a mount that reads nothing there. Clear Host (and
       HostAsked), or use KindGraft if you meant to clone that path.

== graft_kindproc_at_the_wrong_path ==
cannot graft /dev into the engine's view: /dev is snug's own: it must be bwrap's synthetic minimal device set, never a bind of the host's (which hands over every block device and every input device).
       A graft at that path would displace it in the ENGINE's mount namespace
       exactly as a profile's grant would displace it in the sandbox's — this is a
       hole no graft may open, snug's own code included. Graft a destination that
       is neither /dev nor an ancestor of it.

== env_name_empty ==
environ.set has an entry with an empty name. A variable with no name cannot be set; delete the line

== env_name_equals ==
environ.set names "PATH=/evil:", which contains '='. NAME=VALUE is the wire format of the environment itself, so a name with '=' in it is a second assignment smuggled inside the first. Use one entry per variable

== env_name_nul ==
environ.set names a variable containing a NUL byte. The environment is a NUL-terminated list, so the name would be truncated at that byte and the remainder read as something else entirely

== env_name_newline ==
environ.set names "EDITOR\\nPS1", which contains a newline. Every --dry-run line and every refusal renders a variable name on one line; a name that spans two makes those unreadable and unparseable

== env_name_leading_digit ==
environ.set names "1PATH", which starts with a digit. A variable name is [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*, and a shell cannot expand a name starting with a digit — $1 is a positional parameter

== env_name_bad_character ==
environ.set names "MY-VAR", which contains "-". A variable name is [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* — the rule execve(2) and every shell already assume. Rename it

== env_name_snug_owned ==
environ.set names SNUG_PROFILES, which snug writes itself. No profile may write a name snug writes: HOME, PATH and SHELL have no safe absent state, PS1 is executed by bash, and SNUG* is what --dry-run is read against — a profile that could set one could lie to the artifact a human reads to decide whether to trust the sandbox. Remove the line

== env_value_c1_csi ==
environ.set on EDITOR has a value containing '\u009b'. Every screen a human reads to decide whether to trust a sandbox renders a value on one line; a control character forges rows in it or erases them from the terminal. Remove it

== env_value_bidi_override ==
environ.set on EDITOR has a value containing '\u202e'. Every screen a human reads to decide whether to trust a sandbox renders a value on one line; a directional formatting character reverses the rest of the line, so it renders as content it does not contain. Remove it

== env_name_snug_owned_ps1 ==
environ.inherit names PS1, which snug writes itself. No profile may write a name snug writes: HOME, PATH and SHELL have no safe absent state, PS1 is executed by bash, and SNUG* is what --dry-run is read against — a profile that could set one could lie to the artifact a human reads to decide whether to trust the sandbox. Remove the line

== env_set_on_a_list ==
environ.set on PATH, which is a list — use environ.merge, or environ.prepend if the order matters. environ.set on a list would replace every other profile's entries, which snug does not allow

== env_merge_on_a_scalar ==
environ.merge on EDITOR, which is a scalar, not a list — use environ.set

== env_merge_on_an_uncomposable_list ==
environ.merge on CDPATH, which snug does not compose. Its elements are not independent — see .claude/design/ENVIRONMENT-VARIABLES.md §3.3 — so joining two profiles' entries would change what the value MEANS rather than lengthen it

== env_inherit_on_a_list ==
environ.inherit on PKG_CONFIG_PATH, which is a list. Inheriting a host search path wholesale imports directories the sandbox does not have — use environ.sanitise, which copies the host value and keeps only the elements policy grants

== env_sanitise_on_a_scalar ==
environ.sanitise on EDITOR, which is a scalar. sanitise filters the ELEMENTS of a host list; for a scalar there is nothing to filter — use environ.inherit to take the host's value, or environ.set to write one

== env_sanitise_on_manpath ==
environ.sanitise on MANPATH, where an empty element is an INSTRUCTION rather than a gap: a leading one prepends the system path, a trailing one appends it, and '::' inserts it in place. Removing an element there can ADD directories, which is the opposite of what a filter is for. Use environ.merge with the directories you mean

== env_sanitise_on_an_unfilterable_list ==
environ.sanitise on PYTHONPATH, which snug refuses to filter: an empty or dropped element changes the meaning of the value rather than shortening it — see .claude/design/ENVIRONMENT-VARIABLES.md §3.3. Use environ.merge with the directories you mean

== env_unrostered_merge ==
environ.merge on MY_TOOL_PATH, which snug has no entry for. A list verb needs the
       separator that variable is read with and what an EMPTY ELEMENT means to its
       consumer — ignored, the current directory, or an instruction that ADDS
       directories (§3.3) — and snug will not guess either from the shape of a value.
       Use environ.set with the whole value, or add a row to
       internal/policy/envtypes.go carrying the separator and the empty-element kind.

== env_separator_in_a_merge_string ==
environ.merge on PATH has the element "/usr/bin:/usr/sbin", which contains ":" — a separator PATH is read with. Write the elements:
         PATH = ["/usr/bin", "/usr/sbin"]
       snug never splits a value on a separator, so a hand-written one can smuggle in an empty element, which in a search path means the current directory

== env_separator_in_a_prepend_element ==
environ.prepend on PATH has the element "/a:/b", which contains ":" — a separator PATH is read with. Write the elements:
         PATH = ["/a", "/b"]
       snug never splits a value on a separator, so a hand-written one can smuggle in an empty element, which in a search path means the current directory

== env_uncoupled_set ==
profile "broken" sets XDG_DATA_HOME=/home/u/.local/share, which it does not grant.
       Add the path to that profile's ro/rw/tmpfs — or to a profile it includes — or
       drop the variable: a variable naming a path that is not inside the sandbox is
       worse than an absent one, because every tool that reads it will believe it.
       snug is not checking that the path EXISTS (it cannot: a tmpfs grant creates an
       empty directory), only that the profile naming it is the profile that granted it.

== env_uncoupled_merge ==
profile "tpath" merges PATH=/nonexistent/bin, which it does not grant.
       Add the path to that profile's ro/rw/tmpfs — or to a profile it includes — or
       drop the variable: a variable naming a path that is not inside the sandbox is
       worse than an absent one, because every tool that reads it will believe it.
       snug is not checking that the path EXISTS (it cannot: a tmpfs grant creates an
       empty directory), only that the profile naming it is the profile that granted it.

== env_uncoupled_despite_another_profile_granting_it ==
profile "namer" merges PATH=/opt/tools/bin, which it does not grant.
       Add the path to that profile's ro/rw/tmpfs — or to a profile it includes — or
       drop the variable: a variable naming a path that is not inside the sandbox is
       worse than an absent one, because every tool that reads it will believe it.
       snug is not checking that the path EXISTS (it cannot: a tmpfs grant creates an
       empty directory), only that the profile naming it is the profile that granted it.

== env_relative_set ==
profile "rel": environ.set CARGO_HOME entry "cargo" must be an absolute path: a relative one is resolved against whatever directory the payload happens to be in, which is not something a profile can know

== env_relative_set_bash_env ==
profile "startup": environ.set BASH_ENV entry ".snug-init.sh" must be an absolute path: a relative one is resolved against whatever directory the payload happens to be in, which is not something a profile can know

== env_relative_set_pointer ==
profile "ptr": environ.set GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM entry "sys.gitconfig" must be an absolute path: a relative one is resolved against whatever directory the payload happens to be in, which is not something a profile can know

== env_relative_set_annotated_path ==
profile "tpl": environ.set GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR entry "tpl" must be an absolute path: a relative one is resolved against whatever directory the payload happens to be in, which is not something a profile can know

== env_two_prepends ==
profiles mytools and othertools prepend to PATH, and they do not agree:
         mytools wants ["/opt/bin"]
         othertools wants ["/srv/bin"]
       Only one profile may hold the front of a variable. Use environ.merge in
       the ones that do not need to be first — a merged entry still beats every
       entry snug adds, so nothing is lost but the guarantee of being first.

== env_prepend_order_disagreement ==
profiles ordera and orderb prepend to PATH, and they do not agree:
         ordera wants ["/opt/a" "/opt/b"]
         orderb wants ["/opt/b" "/opt/a"]
       Only one profile may hold the front of a variable. Use environ.merge in
       the ones that do not need to be first — a merged entry still beats every
       entry snug adds, so nothing is lost but the guarantee of being first.

== env_two_sets_disagree ==
profiles seta, setb and setc disagree about MY_EDITOR:
         setb (environ.set) says "emacs"
         seta (environ.set) says "vim"
         setc (environ.set) says "vim"
       A scalar has one value and snug will not choose: picking one would make
       the answer depend on the order profiles were folded, and the model has no
       such order. Select one of them, or make them agree.

== env_set_disagrees_with_inherit ==
profiles emacsy and envy disagree about EDITOR:
         emacsy (environ.set) says "emacs"
         envy (environ.inherit) says "vim"
       A scalar has one value and snug will not choose: picking one would make
       the answer depend on the order profiles were folded, and the model has no
       such order. Select one of them, or make them agree.
